ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A string of small lanterns (five) are connected to each other by light strings and suspended in the air. Under the action of a steady horizontal wind force, they tilt, and the angle between the string and the vertical direction is $30^{\circ}$, as shown in the figure. Suppose the mass of each lantern is $m$. Find the magnitude of the pulling force exerted by the first lantern from top to bottom on the second lantern.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a vertical dashed line as a vertical reference line; five small lanterns are strung together by light strings along the same inclined direction, and the whole is inclined toward the lower right; 30° is marked between the top string segment and the vertical direction. From the figure, the string segment between the first and second lanterns from top to bottom is located between them; if this string segment is taken as the action boundary, it bears the four lanterns below, from the second to the fifth. Reasoning: Take the whole composed of the second to the fifth lanterns from top to bottom as the object of study. The total weight of this whole is 4mg, directed vertically downward; the steady horizontal wind force only provides a horizontal action and does not participate in vertical equilibrium. The first lantern exerts a pulling force T on the second lantern through the middle light string; the direction of the pulling force is along the string and makes an angle of 30° with the vertical direction, so its vertical component is T cos30°. From vertical equilibrium, T cos30° = 4mg. Substituting cos30° = √3/2 gives T = 4mg / (√3/2) = 8mg/√3 = 8√3mg/3.
